title: Spin-cQED with bulk germanium spin qubits
authors: A. -F. Kalo, E. A. Rodríguez-Mena, J. C. Abadillo-Uriel, M. Filippone, Y. -M. Niquet
abstract: Unstrained bulk germanium is a particularly attractive material for circuit quantum electrodynamics with spins (spin-cQED). We show, through systematic modeling and comparison with state-of-the-art strained germanium heterostructures, that hole spins in bulk germanium double quantum dots readily reach the strong-coupling regime with superconducting microwave resonators, achieving spin-photon coupling strengths $g_s/2π\gtrsim100$\,MHz. This enhancement originates from large spin-orbit interactions beyond the perturbative regime. In addition, the coupling is much less sensitive to the orientation of the applied magnetic field, which shall ease operation and limit the impact of device-to-device variability. Our results establish bulk germanium as a compelling platform for scalable spin-cQED.
summary: The paper investigates using bulk germanium as a superior material for spin-cQED qubits compared to strained heterostructures. By modeling the system's complex spin physics using the Luttinger–Kohn Hamiltonian, the authors show that hole spins in bulk Ge can achieve strong coupling ($g_s \gtrsim 100$ MHz) with microwave resonators. This makes bulk germanium a highly promising and scalable platform for quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is achieving strong spin-photon coupling ($g_s$) for scalable solid-state quantum computation using hole spins in semiconductor double quantum dots coupled to microwave resonators (spin-cQED).
main_result: Unstrained bulk germanium is established as a compelling platform, showing that hole spins can reach strong coupling regimes with superconducting resonators, achieving $g_s/2\pi \gtrsim 100$ MHz.
method: The analysis involves systematic modeling using the Luttinger–Kohn Hamiltonian to derive an effective spin-photon Hamiltonian and calculate coupling strengths by diagonalizing these models.
model_or_system: The system uses hole spins in double quantum dots (DQD) within bulk germanium, compared against strained heterostructures. The physics is governed by the LK Hamiltonian, which accounts for strong spin-orbit interactions mixing heavy-hole and light-hole states.
key_observables: Spin-photon coupling strength ($g_s/2\pi$), spin-flip tunnel matrix element ($t_{sf}/	ext{2}\pi$), and sensitivity to magnetic field orientation ($\mathbf{B}$).
important_parameters: Achievable $g_s \gtrsim 100$ MHz; the enhancement originates from SO interactions beyond the perturbative regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes operating at zero detuning ($\epsilon = 0$) and relies on deriving an effective Hamiltonian by treating strong spin-orbit coupling effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate device setups comparing strained QWs to unstrained bulk structures, showing the mechanism of spin-photon coupling via hybridization, and detailing $g_s$ dependence on $\mathbf{B}$ orientation for both platforms.
paper_structure: The paper systematically models the system using the LK Hamiltonian, derives an effective spin-photon Hamiltonian, compares results between strained and bulk Ge structures, and concludes by establishing bulk Ge as a superior platform due to higher coupling strengths and reduced field dependence.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses solid-state quantum computing hardware by demonstrating a high-performance qubit platform (Ge hole spins) capable of strong interaction with superconducting cavities, which is central to circuit QED architectures.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Device for spin-photon coupling. (a) The strained QW device. Germanium is colored in red, Ge0.8Si0.2 in blue and the aluminium gates in gray. The 20-nm-thick gates are arranged on two levels separated from each other and from the heterostructure by 6 nm of Al2O3: the barrier (T) and side gates (Sn) on the first level, and the plunger gates PL and PR on the second (diameter 130 nm; distance between cen- ters 170 nm). A resonator with frequency fr and zero-point fluctuations Vzpf is connected to PL. In the bulk heterostruc- ture the buffer and QW are replaced by an unstrained Ge substrate. The yellow shapes are the iso-density surfaces that enclose 20% and 80% of the L and R orbitals....

FIG. 2. Spin-photon coupling in (a-d) a strained Ge QW and (e-h) an unstrained, bulk Ge heterostructure: (a, e) Spectrum of the DQD as a function of detuning energy ε (B ∥x). The resonator couples to the hole in the |−↑⟩and |−↓⟩states; (b, f) Spin-photon coupling gs, (c, g) spin-flip tunnel coupling tsf, (d, h) magnetic field amplitude at resonance (ωs/2π = 2 GHz) as a function of the orientation of B (see Fig. 1). The red cross highlights the optimal orientation B ∥x. In the strained Ge QW, VL = VR = −20.5 mV and VT = −5 mV (all side gates grounded), while in the bulk Ge heterostructure, VL = VR = −43.4 mV and VT = −11.6 mV (top and bottom side gates bias VS1 = VS2 = VS3 = VS4 = 30 mV).

Spintronics.note: The paper directly addresses the interface between quantum optics (spin-photon coupling, cQED) and solid-state magnetism/spins by achieving strong spin-photon coupling ($g_s$) in a semiconductor platform.
